chats.answer:
For a 13-inch laptop, I’d prioritize a 13–14-inch portable monitor with its own stand. It gives you a similarly sized second screen without putting extra weight on a small laptop’s lid and hinges. If you specifically want a screen that attaches to the laptop, fit and mounting weight matter more than the advertised screen size.

My picks

Mobile Pixels DUEX Plus DS 13.3-inch

Best attached screen extender

$159.79

Walmart - ComputerSmartTechs

A 1080p screen that slides out from magnetic mounting plates on your laptop lid. Designed for 13–14.5-inch laptops and weighs about 1.3 lb. Check your lid dimensions before buying. 
The Dad Sneeze

Lenovo ThinkVision M14d

Best overall for work

$251.99

Walmart - ThinkProducts

A freestanding 14-inch, 2240 × 1400 display. Its sharper resolution and taller 16:10 shape make it my choice for code, documents and spreadsheets. Requires video-capable USB-C.

Lenovo ThinkVision M14t Gen 2

Best if you want touch

$318.32

Target

Similar sharp 14-inch workspace, with touchscreen input. Worth the premium only if you'll use touch and your operating system supports it.

I’d buy the DUEX Plus DS if attachment is essential; otherwise, the M14d. I assumed you want one additional screen for productivity, rather than a two-screen attachment or gaming display. These are researched picks, not hands-on tests, and I can't confirm physical fit or port compatibility without your exact laptop model.

What 13-inch laptop do you have—MacBook Air, Dell XPS, Surface, or something else?
